//: Not a build step - DisPatch ships vanilla ES modules with no bundler, and that is deliberate. This file exists so `node --test frontend/tests/` can import those same modules directly instead of a copy: without it node resolves .js as CommonJS and the import fails. The ONE devDependency is jsdom, which several suites need to exercise the DOM half of the app; without it those tests SKIP, and a skipped security test is not a passing one - see CI_REQUIRE_DOM below. The shipped app still installs nothing.

scripts.//test: A glob, not the bare directory: `node --test tests/` resolves the path as a module entry on node >=24 and dies with MODULE_NOT_FOUND before running a single test — which node then reports as one failing test named `tests`, so the suite looked red for a reason that had nothing to do with the code. Node expands this pattern itself; keep it quoted so the shell does not.
scripts.//test:ci: Same suite, with CI_REQUIRE_DOM=1 so a missing jsdom FAILS instead of skipping 60 tests in silence. Use this in automation.

//devDependencies: jsdom only, and only for tests. It is never imported by anything under static/, so it cannot reach a user.
